name: Reset
summary: A reset takes the pace off a hard ball and drops it softly into the opponents' kitchen, turning an attack back into a dinking rally. It is the shot that lets you survive the transition zone and the one that separates players who get pushed off the net from players who do not.
whenToUse: A drive or speed-up is coming at you and counter-attacking is not on.
You are caught in the transition zone with a ball dropping at your feet.
You have just been lobbed or pushed back and want the rally neutral again.
Your partner is out of position and the team needs one slow ball to recover.
howTo: Get low early — the paddle has to be under the ball, not on top of it.
Hold the grip loose. A tight grip is what makes a hard ball rebound.
Meet the ball out in front with the face slightly open and almost no swing.
Absorb rather than hit: let the paddle give a little on contact.
Aim high enough to clear the net and land in the first few feet of their kitchen.
Take one or two steps forward if the reset is good, and split-step again.
commonMistakes: Swinging at it, which sends a fast ball back faster.
Gripping tightly, so the ball springs off the face and floats long.
Standing tall and blocking downward into the net.
Resetting and then rushing forward before the ball has landed.
Backing up to give yourself room, which puts you deeper in the transition zone every rally.

drills.name: Reset from the middle
drills.description: Stand in the transition zone. Your partner drives at you from the kitchen line, hard but at a catchable height. You reset every ball into their kitchen. No swinging is allowed — if the ball goes past the kitchen line, it does not count.

drills.name: Walk and reset
drills.description: Start at the baseline and walk toward the kitchen while your partner drives at you. Reset every ball on the way in, split-stepping each time. You are training the shot in the position you will actually need it.

mistake.label: Blocked with a firm grip: it rebounds off the face, sails past the kitchen and lands at a comfortable height.
